assessment: The 99 is frozen as-played, so all ten are future unlocks ranked by what each would measurably buy. The top two are the diagnosis's own standing adds: the artifact class is zero by enumeration of all 80 entries and fast mana is the smallest, lowest-rated engine class at 43.6%. Ranks 3-9 extend verified architecture — three picks add two-card lines with drains already in the 99, two answer the commander gate that KILL D, E and F all pay, two thicken the death-to-mana class. The tenth closes nothing any measure names and says so out loud. Every bracket figure was recomputed with bracket.assess: floor 4 before and 4 after, on all ten.

ten.why: A turn-two Grafdigger's Cage blanks the Gravecrawler recasts under KILL A and B and every undying return under D and F, and nothing among the 80 entries destroys or exiles an artifact at any price; Gate kills the Cage on your next upkeep for a body the nine-drain layer already pays you to sacrifice.
ten.unlocks: The artifact class, repeatably, for two mana — the corpus says to 'cover the classes — creature, artifact, enchantment, graveyard, land — before doubling any', and artifact is the binding zero. Marginal frame: breadth goes 2 to 3 with this card and moves for no other card on this list. It is an enchantment, so Cursed Totem cannot switch off the thing that answers it. Priced honestly: your upkeep only, once each turn, so a resolved hoser gets one full rotation before it dies.

ten.why: Fast mana is the smallest and lowest-rated multi-card engine class — three cards, 43.6% drawn, the reason Yawgmoth lands on turn 2 in only 7.2% of sims — and Culling converts a body the deck draws in 82.3% of games into BBBB for one mana, a turn-2 commander or a same-turn Nest-plus-drain deploy.
ten.unlocks: The turn the engine comes online moves up one: sacrifice the Stitcher's Supplier that already did its job and cast Yawgmoth with a Swamp open. The sacrifice is itself a death trigger for the drain layer. Stated cost: it carries ramp:ritual, so the ramp axis goes 12 to 13, one over the 10-12 window.

ten.closes: engine component: Exquisite Blood (KILL C's sole amplifier half)
ten.why: KILL C is the deck's best commander-free kill (mean turn 5.1, 42.6% assisted) and its 'opponent loses, you gain' half is one card, Exquisite Blood, at 6.6% unassisted; Bloodthirsty Conqueror is the same text on a 5/5 flying deathtoucher and pairs into a two-card loop with three drains already sleeved.
ten.unlocks: Three new two-card lines with Marauding Blight-Priest, Starscape Cleric and South Wind Avatar — each the KILL C architecture with a second copy of the scarce half, so a graveyard lock that blanks the recursion kills leaves two amplifiers and three triggers instead of one and three. None is verified; each needs a stack scenario before it is claimed as a kill.

ten.why: Three of the six declared kills (D, E, F) need Yawgmoth on the battlefield, KILL E's 38.9% assisted by-turn-6 rate assumes he survives a rotation, and exactly three cards can carry him through a removal spell; Imp's Mischief bends a Swords to Plowshares onto another body at instant speed in a colour that cannot counter it.
ten.unlocks: Marginal frame: it carries protection:redirect, so the axis the diagnosis calls a weakness goes 3 to 4 — the only card on this list the protection count credits. It also guards the other one-of the engine leans on: a targeted Nature's Claim on Nest of Scarabs, KILL E's irreplaceable piece, is a single-target spell and can be pushed elsewhere. Priced honestly: you lose life equal to the redirected spell's mana value, and it redirects only single-target spells.

ten.closes: engine component: Yawgmoth on the engine turn (a kill that does not need him)
ten.why: Every current Mikaeus kill also needs the commander or a sac outlet on the board; Ballista plus Mikaeus alone is infinite pings at the table — remove the last counter, it dies at 0/0, undying returns it — so the deck gains a two-card kill that pays no commander tax when Yawgmoth has died twice.
ten.unlocks: A removal piece and a mana sink stapled to a combo half: early it snipes a Viscera Seer's mirror or an Esper Sentinel, late every spare BB becomes counters. Read honestly: it carries no wincon role, so threat-density does not see it and no counted axis moves — this pick is bought entirely on the Mikaeus line, which needs a stack scenario before it is claimed.

ten.why: A ninth free repeatable outlet (the class sits at 78.5%) that is itself a two-card kill with Mikaeus — sacrifice him to his own undying, mill a library out — and a third piece the Gravecrawler + Pitiless Plunderer loop can route through when Warren Soultrader is answered.
ten.unlocks: Three contained loops, including one that turns Pawn of Ulamog and Reassembling Skeleton into infinite mana and Treasure. Outside the combo it fills your own graveyard for Agadeem's Awakening and Phyrexian Reclamation, and it synergizes with Woe Strider's goat tokens as free fodder. Mill as a win reads honestly: one library at a time unless a loop is running.

ten.why: The death-to-mana class is what makes a sacrifice loop mana-positive rather than merely free, and Sifter is a second Pawn of Ulamog — every nontoken death banks a sacrificial Scion that is both a colorless mana and one more body for Yawgmoth to spend.
ten.unlocks: Seven contained lines, including a three-card loop with Reassembling Skeleton and Phyrexian Altar and a four-card near-infinite draw engine with the commander, Zulaport Cutthroat and Butcher Ghoul. Read honestly before buying: 'another nontoken creature' — Bitterblossom, Ophiomancer and Grave Titan tokens do not trigger it, so it is narrower here than its text looks in a creature deck.

ten.why: A tenth renewable-fodder source that recurs for B every time another creature dies — trivially every turn here — and both partners of its infinite-mana line, Phyrexian Altar and Pawn of Ulamog, are already sleeved.
ten.unlocks: Two contained loops producing infinite colored mana and death triggers, plus a shadow body that connects for commander-damage chip when boards stall. Said plainly, because oracle text settles it: this is NOT Gravecrawler redundancy — Traitor triggers only when ANOTHER creature dies, so it cannot loop by sacrificing itself, and Gravecrawler's 17.0% single-point rate is untouched by this pick. Stitcher's Supplier milling it to the yard is a discount, not a cost.

ten.why: In this deck life is the real spell resource — Yawgmoth's draw, Necropotence, Ancient Tomb and two Phyrexian pips all charge it — and a one-drop that banks a life for every creature death, yours or the table's, refuels roughly four activations a turn once the engine runs.
ten.unlocks: Longer Yawgmoth chains on grind turns and a safer Necropotence number at end of turn. Ranked last on purpose, and honestly: it carries only threat:body, no counted axis moves for it, and it closes nothing the diagnosis names — it holds a slot on this list because roughly half the commander's community lists run it, and the strongest thing this page can do with a famous card the measures cannot see is say exactly that.

gaps: Nest of Scarabs redundancy: KILL E's engine piece is a one-of with no mono-black functional substitute in the pool, so no add on this list raises its 8% unassisted assembly — the protective answer here is Imp's Mischief (rank 4) plus the existing tutors; a true second copy of the effect does not exist to recommend.
Drivnod halving the undying-pair loop's ~30 activations extends a checker-passed stack with an unverified interaction; settled by /resolve-stack before it is ever presented as a kill-speed claim.

Every combo line above is index-derived and marked 'needs a stack scenario'; the Walking Ballista + Mikaeus and Bloodthirsty Conqueror pairs are the two whose verification would most change the deck's declared kill table.
Deathgreeter's community inclusion figure comes from deck_recon.json, whose staleness is time-based, not input-based; a fresh recon pass would re-settle it.
